failures.message: Executor terminated before the lap boundary

conclusions.finding: No SAC improvement over BC incumbent in the frozen R5/R6 evidence
conclusions.evidence: All nine SAC cases selected episode zero; gain_over_bc_s=0, SAC_improvement_found=false. Last checkpoints are separate and slower.
conclusions.implication: Successful legal fallback is BC preservation, not SAC success or learning convergence.

conclusions.finding: Critic values remain inconsistent with realised long-horizon returns
conclusions.evidence: R5 final Q-MC RMSE38.763–41.258 seconds; R6 final37.596–38.641 seconds. R6 positive Q-minus-realised-soft-MC31.741–32.975 seconds despite twin-Q disagreement0.046–0.077 seconds.
conclusions.implication: Small TD loss or twin-critic agreement cannot certify correct total return. Realised stochastic MC comparisons diagnose value mismatch; they do not alone estimate exact policy-expectation bias.

conclusions.finding: R6 modestly improves final policies but still fails learning and fidelity gates
conclusions.evidence: Every R6 last policy is faster than matching R5 fixed last, but slower than matching BC; calibration mean RMSE19.829–20.287km/h, max sector errors1.307–1.681seconds.
conclusions.implication: MC initialisation plus potential sensitivity is a joint experiment; individual causal effects cannot be separated and no convergence is demonstrated.

conclusions.finding: Reward does not purchase pace with terminal SOC bonus
conclusions.evidence: gamma1, elapsed seconds objective, terminal potential zero including failed prefix; every R6 training trajectory potential total is numerically zero. The one failed episode has explicit−100seconds failure penalty.
conclusions.implication: Potential redistribution changes local credit, not complete-episode elapsed-time objective. It does not itself ensure optimal policy or correct Q.

conclusions.finding: Observed model discrepancy precedes resumed ML
conclusions.evidence: R0 historical training_run=false; baseline cal RMSE21.041km/h. R1 power-responsive execution reduces it to19.738 while keeping periodic speed/DC/FSM boundaries.
conclusions.implication: The frozen pre-v6 model error should not be attributed to SAC. Geometry/line, ICE/ERS uncertainty and equivalent model parameters still constrain truthfulness.

conclusions.finding: Physical and boundary checks must be assessed separately from supervised loss and training completion
conclusions.evidence: R4/2027 raw action RMSE0.01066 still terminates early; 179 complete training laps start103m/s and fail periodic speed closure. Formal evaluations shoot policy-specific initial speed around77.794m/s; no within-lap velocity resets.
conclusions.implication: Partial terminal time is not lap time. Same executor does not imply identical boundary condition; fixed-initial checkpoint roundtrip cannot be called independent shooting parity.

conclusions.finding: Fastest is bounded by the finite research family
conclusions.evidence: R2 recorded numerical incumbent71.032060s; R3 teacher71.033308s; best BC71.043716s. Signed24trial and mode-aware32trial searches are finite, without global-optimality proof.
conclusions.implication: Do not call BC/SAC the fastest sustainable solution or claim millisecond differences as numerically resolved physics. The conservative energy floor/tail mask and disabled positive-wheel superclipping are experiment restrictions.
